hints.content: The arrow points to all values greater than $-4$.
And the point at $-4$ is filled in.
So, the inequality represents everything **greater than or equal to $-4$.**

question.content:
**Choose the inequality that represents the following graph.**



[[☃ image 1]]

[[☃ radio 1]]

options.alt: A number line from negative 5 to 5 with evenly spaced tick marks in increments of 1. A line going to the right starts at negative 4 and continues right. A closed point is plotted at negative 4 where the line begins.

choices.clue:
The graph of $x < -4$ actually looks like this:

![A number line from negative 5 to 5 with evenly spaced tick marks in increments of 1. A line going to the left starts at negative 4 and continues left. An open point is plotted at negative 4 where the line begins.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/9b1561e5c59b3ec47d3b57a7f1ea901aa949e2b1)

The graph of $x \leq-4$ actually looks like this:

![A number line from negative 5 to 5 with evenly spaced tick marks in increments of 1. A line going to the left starts at negative 4 and continues left. A closed point is plotted at negative 4 where the line begins.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/83102ab585a02be22f5b18c8e87dfa0bb5016550)

The graph of $x > -4$ actually looks like this:

![A number line from negative 5 to 5 with evenly spaced tick marks in increments of 1. A line going to the right starts at negative 4 and continues right. An open point is plotted at negative 4 where the line begins.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/83885058c182ad4d8d8bd5a5d793715a44198efd)
